title: Microdash anomaly lens and derivative metrics playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact playbook for building small, focused dashboard "micro-lenses" that accelerate operator triage of inference anomalies. Goal is to codify a small set of derivative metrics and visualization patterns that are cheap to compute, low-cardinality, and high-signal for common failure modes (kv cold-starts, bursty token latency, model fallbacks, routing cascades).

Scope / audience:
- SREs and oncall operators who need fast root-cause hypotheses.
- Observability engineers creating microdash widgets and panels.
- Solutions/SEs preparing customer-facing incident summaries.

High-level heuristics (operator lens):
- Keep slices <= 7 per microdash. Too many panes dilutes investigations.
- Prefer ratios of two primitives rather than new counters (better stability under ingestion variance).
- Always include a single-trace-link anchor (trace id + minimal context) for each anomalous cell.
- Prefer rolling 5m and 1h views together so operators can see spike shape vs sustained drift.

Key derivative metrics (recipes):
1) kv_warmth_index (per-tenant, per-model):
- numerator = unique prefix hits in last 5m (prefix_hit_count)
- denominator = unique prefixes seen across last 1h (prefix_unique_1h)
- kv_warmth_index = numerator / max(denominator, 1)
- Interpretation: ~1 means warm; <0.2 suggests cold cache churn likely causing token latency spikes.
- Notes: use set-approx (count-min sketch) for memory efficiency; mark as approximate in UI.

2) token_latency_tail_ratio (per-route):
- p95_tokens = median token latency at 95th percentile (token-latency/p95)
- p50_tokens = median token latency at 50th percentile
- token_latency_tail_ratio = p95_tokens / max(p50_tokens, 1ms)
- Interpretation: >4 => heavy tail, consider tracing top sessions.

3) model_variant_fallback_rate (global or per-tenant):
- count fallback events / total generation requests over rolling 30m
- Tag by fallback_reason (OOM, timeout, unavailable) to prioritize fixes.

4) small-input-penalty (batching inefficiency index):
- numerator = total batches where avg_input_length < 32 tokens (last 10m)
- denominator = total batches (last 10m)
- recipe: small-input-penalty = numerator/denominator
- Use to detect when customers are sending many tiny prompts causing throughput/cost inefficiency.

5) estimated_per-token-cost (derived):
- input_token_cost = request_input_tokens * avg_cost_per_input_token(model)
- output_token_cost = request_output_tokens * avg_cost_per_output_token(model)
- estimated_per_token_cost = (input_token_cost + output_token_cost) / max(total_tokens,1)
- Useful for cost-aware alerting: flag if estimated_per_token_cost increases > 30% vs baseline.

Visualization patterns (microdash building blocks):
- Compact heatmap: tenant x 5m-bucket of kv_warmth_index (color: cold->hot). Quick visual cue for tenants affected by cold cache.
- Small-multiples lineset: token_latency_tail_ratio across top-10 routes (log y-axis). Use sparklines for mobile.
- Fraction bar: model_variant_fallback_rate broken down by reason. Clickable to open trace sample.
- Cohort scatter: small-input-penalty vs estimated_per_token_cost by tenant. Highlight outliers above cost threshold.

Trace anchoring and span design notes:
- Add a short trace anchor consisting of: request_id, route, model_variant, kv_shard_id (if available). Display prominently in widget hover.
- Instrumentation tip: add a span tag 'kv_hit' = true/false on model inference spans to filter traces with cold cache easily.
- Capture a compact span sample (first 3 spans + final generation span) for microdash preview to reduce trace retrieval costs.

Sampling strategy for microdash panels:
- Adaptive sparse sampling: keep full samples for top 2 tenants by QPS, sample 5% for rest; on detected anomaly bump to 50% for 30m.
- Event-driven capture: when token_latency_tail_ratio > threshold, capture traces for top-5 sessions by latency.

Alerting guidance (sane defaults):
- kv_warmth_index per-tenant < 0.15 sustained for 15m => SEV2 investigation (likely cache churn).
- token_latency_tail_ratio > 6 for any production route for 10m => page SRE and attach microdash view.
- model_variant_fallback_rate > 1% increase over baseline (24h) => ticket to model-onboarding and runtime teams.

Operational runbook snippets (to include in widget):
- Step 1: open heatmap, isolate tenant with low warmth index.
- Step 2: switch to cohort scatter; if tenant has high small-input-penalty, ask engineering to batch or throttle front-end.
- Step 3: open sample traces (anchor) and look for 'kv_miss' spans and downstream queueing.
- Step 4: if fallback_reason == timeout, check upstream network metrics and model-serving CPU/GPU steal.

Cost & query budget considerations:
- Microdash queries should default to 5s timeout and reduced cardinality (pre-aggregated where possible).
- Prefer pre-computed derivative metrics in TSDB to ad-hoc SQL. If computation is expensive, run offline and surface results as a cached widget.

Widget ownership and lifecycle:
- Each microdash must have an owner + fallback owner. Annotate in widget metadata.
- Review microdash list quarterly; retire ones with <5 uses per month.

Small style guide for microdash panels:
- Titles must include the lens name and default time window (e.g., "KV Warmth (5m/1h)").
- Avoid more than 3 color categories for heatmaps. Use colorblind-friendly palette.
- Show sample trace link on hover and a one-line sample explanation of suspected cause (auto-generated by rules).

Example investigation vignette (short):
- Symptom: sudden drop in per-route P99 and concurrent spike in cost.
- Microdash view: heatmap shows tenant X with kv_warmth_index = 0.08; cohort scatter shows small-input-penalty at 0.86; fallback_rate unchanged.
- Root cause hypothesis: frontend changed to send many tiny prompts after a library upgrade, causing inefficient batching and cache churn.
- Next action: roll back change or add client-side batching; monitor microdash for improvement.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define acceptable approximation budget for sketches used in kv_warmth_index (memory vs error tolerance).
- How to surface multi-tenant correlation (cross-tenant noise) without exposing PII? Need policy guidance.
- Should microdash panels include a 1-click ‘replay prompt sample’ sandbox? Security concerns.

Notes to self (drafty):
- Build a sample widget template repository under obs-widgets. Link to PR in linked_artifacts.
- Run a small experiment Q1: deploy microdash for 10 pilot customers and measure median time-to-diagnosis improvement.

References and quick links:
- Confluence: Microdash Catalog (linked above).
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-4121 (microdash ownership sweep).
- GitHub: obs-widgets PR/87 (template for heatmap).

If you take this forward: pick two derivative metrics to compute next week (kv_warmth_index + token_latency_tail_ratio) and add to our TSDB as first-class series. Then convert one existing long dashboard into 3 microdash panels using the patterns above.

Unresolved: need consensus on sample retention policy for trace anchors (30d vs 7d).

-- Samira
